items.title: Usage frequency predicts lexicalization across languages
items.author: Charles Kemp
items.content: Why do almost all human languages have a word for ‘sun’, but fewer have a word for ‘weather’? Khishigsuren et al. find that the usefulness of a concept in communication predicts how often it appears in vocabularies across languages.

items.title: Causal role of human hippocampus in relational structure learning and inference
items.author: Matthew F. S. Rushworth
items.content: Pan and colleagues show that the human hippocampus represents relational structures that support inference in changing environments and provide causal evidence that disrupting hippocampal activity impairs this ability.

items.title: Equitable funding for inclusive big team science
items.author: Kimberly C. Doell
items.content: Big team science seeks to make research more inclusive, but the cost of recruiting representative samples can vary markedly across countries. This risks reinforcing the very inequalities these collaborations seek to address. Pooling resources and asking funders to contribute according to their financial capacity could help to overcome these inequalities.

items.title: Long-term training continually fine tunes motor memories
items.content: Humans’ rapid adaptation to new dynamics is a crucial ability for interacting with the world. By combining the controlled manipulations of sensorimotor adaptation studies with the long-term learning approach of complex tasks, this study shows that the learned motor memory is continually tuned, and that retention increases with long-term training.

items.title: A natural field experiment on the effectiveness of economic sanctions before and after the Russian invasion of Ukraine
items.author: J. C. Sharman
items.content: A field experiment by Findley et al. finds that financial sanctions on Russian officials had little effect on access to banking and corporate services before the 2022 invasion of Ukraine, but significantly reduced access afterwards.

items.title: Long-term development of a motor memory
items.author: Sae Franklin
items.content: Franklin et al. examine how simple motor adaptation is developed with thousands of training trials over multiple weeks to study the long-term development of a motor memory.

items.title: AI ‘slop’ is a social judgement
items.author: Chenhao Tan
items.content: Artificial intelligence (AI)-generated content increasingly saturates our information environment. Efforts to detect and remove it are failing. We propose that calling AI-generated content ‘slop’ is best understood as a social judgement: what a community recognizes as unwanted AI content. Studying AI slop this way makes it tractable, measurable and governable.

items.title: Preprimary education laws and women’s empowerment later in life
items.content: Across nearly 6.7 million women in 117 low- and middle-income countries, eligibility under national preprimary education laws was associated with higher educational enrolment and completion, more gender-egalitarian attitudes, more favourable empowerment-related behaviours and greater reproductive autonomy.
